# Firmware
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/firmware

{/* Generated by `yarn task docs` (firmware command catalog). Do not edit by hand. */}

Firmware is how Zed Cafe turns `#command` text into work: books and pages in the terminal, boards and objects while a world runs, and imports while content loads.

## Drivers

| Driver | When | Firmwares |
|--------|------|-----------|
| **CLI** | Terminal / operator input | `cli` + standard library |
| **LOADER** | Importing files into books | `loader` + standard library |
| **RUNTIME** | Codepage chips on a board | `runtime` + standard library |

**Standard library** (every driver): `audio`, `board`, `network`, `transform`, `element`. Permission checks apply to the **CLI** driver only.

Module notes: [CLI](/firmware/cli) · [Runtime](/firmware/runtime) · [Loader](/firmware/loader).

| Doc | Purpose |

# Audio
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/firmware/audio

**Purpose**: Defines `AUDIO_FIRMWARE` — commands for audio synthesis, playback, text-to-speech (TTS), and effects. Wraps the synth device API for use from user codepages.

{/* firmware-catalog:end */}

## Command Categories

### Text-to-Speech

#### #ttsengine

**Args:** [ `engine` [, `config` ] ]

List engines (no args) or set TTS engine and optional config.

#### #tts

**Args:** [voice] [, phrase]

Speak phrase with voice; no args = clear queue; voice only = info.

#### #ttsqueue

**Args:** `voice`, `phrase`

Queue TTS text.

#### #ttsvol

**Args:** `volume`

Set TTS volume.

Example:

```
#ttsengine
#tts default hello
#ttsqueue default next line
#ttsvol 0.8
```

### Playback

#### #play

**Args:** [buffer]

Play audio buffer (can reference chip variable).

#### #bgplay

**Args:** [buffer]

Play background audio.

#### #vol

**Args:** `volume`

Set main volume (scales all audio).

#### #playvol

**Args:** `volume`

Set foreground play volume.

#### #bgvol

**Args:** `volume`

Set background playback volume.

#### #mediavol

**Args:** `volume`

Set board TV volume.

Example:

```
#play ceg
#bgplay #xyzzy
#vol 0.7
#mediavol 0.5
```

### Synthesis

#### #synth

**Args:** [voice config…]

Configure all 4 play voices; no args = restart synth.

#### #synth1 … #synth4

**Args:** [config…]

Configure individual play voices.

#### #synth5

**Args:** [config…]

Configure background synth voices (4–8).

#### #synthrecord

**Args:** [filename]

Record synth output.

#### #synthflush

**Args:** —

Flush synth buffer.

Example:

```
#synth
#synth1 buzz
#synth5 pad
#synthrecord take1
#synthflush
```

### Effects (multi-voice)

#### #echo

Echo on voices 0–1.

#### #fcrush

Bitcrush (fc) on voices 0–1.

#### #autofilter

Autofilter on voices 0–1.

#### #reverb

Reverb on voices 0–1.

#### #distort

Distortion on voices 0–1.

#### #vibrato

Vibrato on voices 0–1.

#### #autowah

Autowah on voices 0–1.

Example:

```
#echo 0.3 0.2
#reverb 0.4
#fcrush 4
```

### Per-voice effects

#### #echo1 … #echo4

Echo on voice pair / bgplay / TTS (`1`–`3` play/bgplay, `4` TTS).

#### #fcrush1 … #fcrush4

Bitcrush on voice pair / bgplay / TTS.

#### #autofilter1 … #autofilter4

Autofilter on voice pair / bgplay / TTS.

#### #reverb1 … #reverb4

Reverb on voice pair / bgplay / TTS.

#### #distort1 … #distort4

Distortion on voice pair / bgplay / TTS.

#### #vibrato1 … #vibrato4

Vibrato on voice pair / bgplay / TTS.

#### #autowah1 … #autowah4

Autowah on voice pair / bgplay / TTS.

Example:

```
#echo1 0.2 0.1
#reverb4 0.5
#fcrush2 3
```

| [`#write`](#write) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | text to board at direction |

## Command Categories

### Board Creation

#### #build

**Args:** `stat` [, `source`]

Calls [`boardbuild`](../../feature/boardbuild.ts) on the sim. Creates a new TEMP board (optionally clones from source). Exit\* stats set bidirectional board exits. Other standard element stats (`p1`, `group`, …) write the new id on the invoking object; arbitrary names write player flags. Missing source or element fails loud (no create/link).

#### #goto

**Args:** `stat` [, x, y]

Resolves destination (passage match / x,y / start) and calls [`memorymoveplayertoboard`](../../memory/playermanagement.ts). Cross-board `#goto` dither-dissolves to black then in on the local client; same-board position moves and edge exits are unchanged (edge exits keep camera pan).

Cross-board placement commands (`put`/`shoot`/`dupe`/`write`/`shove`/`push` with over/under dirs, etc.) run on the sim against live MEMORY — no worker hydration waits.

Example:

```
#build nextroom
#goto nextroom 10 12
```

### Element Placement

#### #put

**Args:** `dir` `kind`

Place element at direction.

#### #putwith

**Args:** `arg` `dir` `kind`

Place element with arg.

#### #oneof

**Args:** `mark` `dir` `kind`

Place only if no object with `mark` exists.

#### #oneofwith

**Args:** `arg` `mark` `dir` `kind`

Oneof with arg.

#### #shoot

**Args:** `dir` [, kind]

Shoot bullet in direction (default: bullet). Respects maxplayershots. Sets `didshoot` on player.

#### #shootwith

**Args:** `arg` `dir` [, kind]

Shoot with arg.

#### #throwstar

**Args:** `dir`

Shoot star bullet (shorthand for `#shoot <dir> star`).

#### #throwstarwith

**Args:** `arg` `dir`

Shoot star with arg.

Example:

```
#put n red solid
#oneof boss e dragon
#shoot e
#throwstar n
```

### Element Manipulation

#### #duplicate / #dupe

**Args:** `dir` `dupedir`

Duplicate element at dir in dupedir direction.

#### #duplicatewith / #dupewith

**Args:** `arg` `dir` `dupedir`

Duplicate with arg.

#### #shove

**Args:** `dir` `movedir`

Move object at dir by movedir delta.

#### #push

**Args:** `dir` `movedir`

Same as shove but only for pushable objects; a given object succeeds at most once per tick.

#### #transport

**Args:** `target`

First open cell along the shoot ray; an opposite-facing same-kind transporter arms the cell past it; requires approach delta match.

#### #change

**Args:** `target` `into`

Change all elements matching **`<group>`** (name or `@group`) to into kind (or empty→put). Into must be a real kind.

#### #write

**Args:** `dir` `color` `text…`

Write colored text on board at direction (E/W/N/S).

Example:

```
#duplicate by shootx shooty by 1 0
#shove e n
#push w e
#change slime empty
#write e yellow HELLO
```

## Safety

- Player kind cannot be put or shot
- Shooting respects `maxplayershots` and yields after shoot
- Ghost elements bypass collision checks
- Pushable objects are shoved before put when blocking

# CLI
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/firmware/cli

For the player-facing list of every `#command`, see [All commands](/firmware#all-commands) (filter by the **C** badge).

**Purpose**: Defines `CLI_FIRMWARE` — command-line interface commands for system management, book/page operations, export, multiplayer, ZNS, and editing tools. Most commands are operator-only.

## Command help in the editor / terminal

Firmware command signatures stay short. Longer inline help for autocomplete hints can be added as Markdown under [`zss/rom/editor/commands/<command>.md`](../../rom/editor/commands/) (bundled via Vite `import.meta.glob` into [`zss/rom/contentmap.ts`](../../rom/contentmap.ts)). The UI reads these through [`commandromhint`](../../screens/tape/commandarghints.ts) (`editor:commands:<lowercase name>`).

## Command Categories

### Messaging

#### #help

**Args:** —

Open reference scroll.

#### #send

**Args:** target, message…

Message to target elements.

#### #shortsend

**Args:** message…

Short-form message (no target keyword).

#### #stat

**Args:** text…

Text in a scroll window.

# Element
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/firmware/element

**Purpose**: Defines `ELEMENT_FIRMWARE` — commands and hooks for element stats, movement, lifecycle, code execution, and player input. Provides the core vocabulary for object behavior.

## Flags / stats

Names used with `#set`, `#clear`, expressions, and `is`. **Access** is whether the element hook persists a write (`Read/write`) or ignores / does not own the write (`Read-only`).

Color, collision, category, and dir **keywords** also resolve through a const map for expressions — those are not stored stats.

### Board

| Name | Access | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `isdark` | Read/write | Board darkness |
| `startx`, `starty` | Read/write | Login spawn cell |
| `over`, `under` | Read/write | Overlay / underlay board refs |
| `palette`, `charset` | Read/write | Graphics page refs |
| `exitnorth`, `exitsouth`, `exitwest`, `exiteast` | Read/write | Edge exits to other boards |
| `timelimit` | Read/write | Board time limit |
| `restartonzap` | Read/write | Restart-on-zap flag |
| `maxplayershots` | Read/write | Cap on player shots |
| `b1` … `b10` | Read/write | Board generic slots |

### Element

| Name | Access | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `char`, `color`, `bg` | Read/write | Instance look; `color`/`bg` accept color words or numbers |
| `displaychar`, `displaycolor`, `displaybg` | Read/write | Display overrides (`:drawdisplay` must set these by name) |
| `displayname` | Read/write | Prefix before `$ticker` text in the gadget ticker strip |
| `item`, `group`, `party`, `player` | Read/write | Identity / grouping |
| `pushable`, `collision`, `breakable` | Read/write | Physics flags |
| `p1` … `p20` | Read/write | Generic numeric params |
| `cycle` | Read/write | Tick rate divisor (1–255) |
| `stepx`, `stepy` | Read/write | Walk deltas (also driven by `#walk`) |
| `shootx`, `shooty` | Read/write | Shoot aim axes |
| `didfail` | Read/write | Last move/action failure flag |
| `light` | Read/write | Radius; get reads `lightsteps`. Set accepts radius and optional dir cone |
| `lightsteps`, `lightx`, `lighty` | Read/write | Light radius and cone axes |
| `arg` | Read/write | Run / with argument bag |

### Env

| Name | Access | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `currenttick` | Read-only | Sim timestamp |
| `boardid` | Read-only | Current board id |
| `playerid` | Read-only | Focused player id |
| `playerx`, `playery` | Read-only | Focused player position |
| `thisid`, `thisx`, `thisy` | Read-only | Current element id / position |
| `kind` | Read-only | Current element kind name |
| `senderid` | Read/write | Get: sender element id. Set: writes `element.sender` |
| `senderx`, `sendery` | Read-only | Sender position |

### Input

Player chips only. Values come from the input queue (`inputmove` / `inputshoot` may list up to two dirs for diagonals; FPV remaps dirs).

| Name | Access | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `inputmove`, `inputshoot` | Read-only | Direction lists from move / shoot |
| `inputok`, `inputcancel`, `inputmenu` | Read-only | Face buttons / menu |
| `inputa`, `inputb`, `inputx`, `inputy` | Read-only | Extra face buttons |
| `inputl1`, `inputl2`, `inputr1`, `inputr2` | Read-only | Shoulder buttons |
| `inputalt`, `inputctrl`, `inputshift` | Read-only | Modifiers |

### Player flags

Open read/write bag on the focused player (`BOOK_FLAGS`). Any name that is not a board/element/env/input hit falls through here. Examples:

| Name | Access | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `health` | Read/write | Player health; ≤ 0 ends the program (see Lifecycle) |
| `user`, `voice` | Read/write | Sticky on the local tab (`register:stickyuser` / `register:stickyvoice`) |
| `camera`, `graphics` | Read/write | Display prefs (player flags; no board fallback on get) |
| `facing` | Read/write | Degrees 0–359; get falls back to board facing if unset |

If a name matches an object id key on the current board, **get** returns that id string (alias). That path is read-only.

## Lifecycle

`aftertick` on element firmware:

- **Walk** — If the element has `stepx` / `stepy`, move it; on blocked move send `:thud`
- **Health** — If player and `health` ≤ 0: end of program and logout

## Commands

### State

#### #set

**Args:** `name` `value`

Set stat (default value 1). Value may be an expr, e.g. `set name pget <dir> <attr>`.

#### #clear

**Args:** stat…

Set listed stats to 0.

#### #pset

**Args:** `<dir>` `attr` `value`

Write remote attr (`step`/`shoot` ← dir → axes; `light <n> [dir]` → lightsteps + cone).

#### #cycle

**Args:** `value`

Set cycle (1–255).

Example:

```
#set health 100
#clear didfail
#pset n step e
#cycle 4
```

### Movement

#### #go

**Args:** `dir`

Move element to dest; yield; return 0 if moved, 1 if blocked.

#### #walk

**Args:** `dir` `[name1 name2]`

Set stepx/stepy, or capture deltas into names.

#### #idle

**Args:** —

Yield until next tick.

Example:

```
#go n
#if didfail
#walk e
#idle
```

### Transformation

#### #become

**Args:** `kind`

Transform into kind (preserve color), delete self, create new, endofprogram.

#### #morph

**Args:** `kind`

Drop code/kinddata, set kind (object source; object or terrain target); halt chip.

#### #bind

**Args:** `name`

Copy kind and instance code from named element; halt chip.

#### #char

**Args:** [dir] `value`

Set char at dir or self.

#### #color

**Args:** [dir] `color`

Set color at dir or self.

Example:

```
#char 2
#color red
#morph lion
#become key
```

### Lifecycle

#### #die

**Args:** —

Safely delete element; if item, yoink player to position; else endofprogram.

#### #end

**Args:** [result]

Set arg if result, endofprogram.

#### #lock

**Args:** —

Lock chip against external messages.

#### #unlock

**Args:** —

Unlock chip against messages from others.

#### #restore

**Args:** `id`

Restore all labels of given name.

#### #zap

**Args:** `id`

Zap (de-activate) first label of given name.

Example:

```
#lock
#zap touch
#restore touch
#unlock
#end
```

### Code Execution

#### #run

**Args:** `func`

Run object codepage of given name.

#### #runwith

**Args:** `arg` `func`

Set arg, run codepage.

#### #load

**Args:** `dir` [, action]

Load code from object at dir; action=append or kind name.

Example:

```
#run helper
#runwith 3 helper
#load n append
```

### Data

#### #array

**Args:** `name` val…

Set stat to array of values.

#### #read

**Args:** `from` `prop` `name`

Read from[prop] into stat.

Example:

```
#array dirs n e s w
#read self color mycolor
```

## Input Handling

`readinput` / `applyinputqueue` drains the player’s input queue each tick: coalesces all `MOVE_*` / `SHOOT_*` into `inputmove` / `inputshoot` (up to two dirs for diagonals, with FPV remap), and applies one button/action (`inputok`, `inputa`, sided ctrl, etc.).

# Loader
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/firmware/loader

For the player-facing list of every `#command`, see [All commands](/firmware#all-commands) (filter by the **L** badge).

**Purpose**: Defines `LOADER_FIRMWARE` — commands for loading and parsing external files (text, JSON, binary) and managing loader context. Used when importing content into books.

## Implementations

`LOADER_FIRMWARE` in [`loader.ts`](../loader.ts) registers `#readline` / `#readjson` / `#readbin` (and media / context commands). The read handlers live under [`loader/`](../loader/):

| Module | Command | Role |
|--------|---------|------|
| [`loader/text.ts`](../loader/text.ts) | `#readline` | Line cursor + regex capture |
| [`loader/json.ts`](../loader/json.ts) | `#readjson` | JMESPath query into a stat |
| [`loader/binary.ts`](../loader/binary.ts) | `#readbin` | Typed binary reads |
| [`loader/media.ts`](../loader/media.ts) | `#media` | Submit URL to board TV helper |
| [`loader/mediaqueueflags.ts`](../loader/mediaqueueflags.ts) | (get hooks) | `mediaqueue` / `medialist` flag lines |

## Flags / stats

Loader get hooks are **read-only**. Copy a value with `#set` before an `is` check when you need a durable local copy.

### Chat / media

These names work for every loader, including a chat loader with no file:

| Name | Access | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| `chatconnected` | Read-only | `1` when the twitch chat slot is connected, else `0` |
| `chatchannel` | Read-only | Channel name |
| `chatusername` | Read-only | Logged-in nick (token user, or the anonymous `justinfan` nick) |
| `mediaqueue` | Read-only | Array of approval rows, `index duration name title` (`3m` or `unknown`; title falls back to the url). Walk with `#foreach` |
| `medialist` | Read-only | Array of play-queue rows, `index name title`. Walk with `#foreach` |

`mediaqueue` and `medialist` read the operator board's media helper. An unbound helper is an empty array.

Loaders can post to twitch with `#chat say <text>`. It always speaks as the operator (the tab that owns the twitch connection), and needs a tokened `#chat <channel> twitchtoken=` session. Other `#chat` forms are CLI only. See `ops/fixtures/lang/coolregionsbow/twitchmedia.zss` (`!media`, `!queue`) for `#foreach` over `medialist` / `mediaqueue` with `#chat say`.

### File metadata

Availability depends on loader format:

| Name | Access | text | json | binary | Notes |
|------|--------|------|------|--------|-------|
| `format` | Read-only | yes | yes | yes | Current loader format |
| `filename` | Read-only | yes | yes | yes | Source file name |
| `cursor` | Read-only | yes | — | yes | Line or byte cursor |
| `lines` | Read-only | yes | — | — | Text line count |
| `bytes` | Read-only | — | — | yes | Binary byte length |
| `eof` | Read-only | yes | — | yes | `1` when cursor is past end |

## Commands

### File readers

#### #readline

**Args:** `<kind> [args…]`

Text line reader — implemented by [`loader/text.ts`](../loader/text.ts).

**seek** — `#readline seek <cursor>` sets the line cursor (0-based). Clamped to `[0, lines]` — **`cursor = lines` is EOF** (one past the last line).

**next** — `#readline next` advances the cursor by one (clamped to EOF).

**Regex capture** — `#readline <regex> <name1> [name2] …`

- Matches `regex` (case-insensitive) against the **current** line
- Capture group 1 → `name1`, group 2 → `name2`, etc.
- Unmatched captures on a real line get `0`
- **Does not advance** — use `#readline next` to move
- On **EOF** (`cursor = lines`): every capture name is set to `''` (empty string)

If line is `42 foo`, `#readline ^(\d+)\s+(\w+)$ count label` sets `count=42`, `label='foo'`. Cursor stays put.

EOF checks: `#while not eof do` / `#if not eof` (readable `eof` flag), or `#if cursor = lines`. On EOF, captures are `''` (vs `0` for a failed match on a real line).

#### #readjson

**Args:** `<jmespath_filter> <name>`

JSON query — implemented by [`loader/json.ts`](../loader/json.ts).

- **filter** — JMESPath expression (e.g. `items[0].name`, `people[*].id`)
- **name** — stat to store the result

See [JMESPath](https://jmespath.org/) for query syntax.

#### #readbin

**Args:** `<kind> [args…]`

Binary reader — implemented by [`loader/binary.ts`](../loader/binary.ts).

**seek** — `#readbin seek <cursor>` sets the binary reader cursor to the given byte index.

**Numeric types** — for each type, reads from the current cursor and stores in the given stat name. Suffix `le` = little-endian.

| Kind | Size | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `float32` / `float32le` | 4 | 32-bit float |
| `float64` / `float64le` | 8 | 64-bit float |
| `int8` / `int8le` | 1 | 8-bit signed |
| `int16` / `int16le` | 2 | 16-bit signed |
| `int32` / `int32le` | 4 | 32-bit signed |
| `int64` / `int64le` | 8 | 64-bit signed (BigInt) |
| `uint8` / `uint8le` | 1 | 8-bit unsigned |
| `uint16` / `uint16le` | 2 | 16-bit unsigned |
| `uint32` / `uint32le` | 4 | 32-bit unsigned |
| `uint64` / `uint64le` | 8 | 64-bit unsigned (BigInt) |

`#readbin uint32 mystat` reads 4 bytes into `mystat`.

**text** — `#readbin text <lengthkind> <target>` reads a length using `lengthkind` (e.g. `uint8`), decodes that many bytes as UTF-8 into `target`, and advances the cursor.

Example:

```
#while not eof do
#readline "^(.*)$" line
#readline next
#done
#readjson title mytitle
#readbin uint32 mystat
#readbin text uint8 str
```

### Media queue

#### #media

**Args:** `<name> <url>`

Submit URL to the board TV helper with explicit queue display name (operator + `speaker` / `media` permission). Prefer `#withplayerboard` or `#withboard` first so the helper resolves from loader targeting. Empty name sanitizes to `player`.

#### #queue

**Args:** (same as CLI `#queue`)

Media queue admin. Runs as the operator (`elementfocus`), so the loader script has to decide who may call it.

#### #chat

**Args:** …

Chat bridge (`#chat say` from loaders; other forms are CLI).

Example:

```
#withplayerboard
#media player https://example.com/clip.mp4
#chat say queue updated
```

### Messaging

#### #send

**Args:** target, message…

Message to target elements.

#### #shortsend

**Args:** message…

Short-form message (no target keyword).

#### #stat

**Args:** text…

Text in a scroll window.

#### #text

**Args:** text…

Text on element or in sidebar.

#### #hyperlink

**Args:** …

Clickable link in scroll or log.

Example:

```
#text loading...
#send all :ready
#stat import done
```

### Context

#### #withboard

**Args:** `stat`

Set READ_CONTEXT.board to board at stat; element = random pt.

#### #withplayerboard

**Args:** —

Cycle next active player's board via `withplayerboard_tracking` shuffle queue; element = random pt.

#### #withobject

**Args:** `id`

Set READ_CONTEXT.element to object; updates elementid, elementisplayer, elementfocus for send/chat.

Example:

```
#withboard nextroom
#withplayerboard
#withobject chatuser
```

### Loader context

#### #endgame

**Args:** —

No-op (avoids ending session during import).

Example:

```
#endgame
```

### Input simulation

#### #userinput

**Args:** `action`

Simulate input: up, down, left, right, shootup/down/left/right, ok, cancel.

Example:

```
#userinput up
#userinput ok
```

## Design notes

- `withobject` enables `#oneof chatuser … #withobject chatuser #goup '` patterns for chat-driven object behavior
- `#withplayerboard` picks among **active** players (activelist + object on board), cycling each pid once through a shuffled `ids` queue under `withplayerboard_tracking` (same pattern as `@pick shuffle`); then sets that player's board. Does not set player focus — use `#withobject` for that
- `#withboard` / `#withplayerboard` / `#withobject` set board and object **targeting** on `READ_CONTEXT`; `memorytickloaders` in [`zss/memory/runtime.ts`](../../memory/runtime.ts) persists those five fields per loader chip id across ticks (not whole `READ_CONTEXT`, not across separate loader invocations)
- Loader `#media <name> <url>` uses `READ_CONTEXT.board` when set (via `#withboard` / `#withplayerboard`), otherwise the operator's player board, for helper resolution
- Loader context overrides runtime behavior for messaging/UI
- `endgame` is no-op in loaders to avoid ending session during import

---

# Network
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/firmware/network

**Purpose**: Defines `NETWORK_FIRMWARE` — commands for HTTP requests. Provides `#fetch` and `#fetchwith` to perform GET or POST requests and handle responses via callbacks.

{/* firmware-catalog:begin */}
{/* Generated by `yarn task docs` (firmware command catalog). Do not edit by hand. */}

<a id="module-commands"></a>

## All commands (2)

<p class="fw-where-legend"> <span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span> CLI - terminal / operator <span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span> Loader - import <span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span> Runtime - codepages </p>

| Command | Where | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| [`#fetch`](#fetch) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | URL with label, method, and optional data |
| [`#fetchwith`](#fetchwith) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | URL with argument, label, method, and optional data |
{/* firmware-catalog:end */}

## Commands

### HTTP

#### #fetch

**Args:** `label` `url` [, method] [args…]

Make HTTP request; `label` is callback target; `method` defaults to `get`.

#### #fetchwith

**Args:** `arg` `label` `url` [, method] [args…]

Same as fetch but passes `arg` to callback.

The `label` is used to route the response to a handler (e.g., a codepage or send target).

Example:

```
#fetch onresponse https://api.example.com/data get
#fetchwith myarg onresponse https://api.example.com/submit post:json x 1 y 2
```

## Supported Methods

Method is optional on `#fetch` / `#fetchwith` and defaults to `get`. Remaining args after the method become request data for methods that take a body.

### get

HTTP GET. Extra args after the URL are ignored by the request.

```
#fetch onresponse https://api.example.com/data get
#fetch onresponse https://api.example.com/data
```

### post:json

HTTP POST with `Content-Type: application/json`. Trailing args are paired as `key value` entries and sent as a JSON object.

```
#fetch onresponse https://api.example.com/submit post:json name alice score 10
#fetchwith myarg onresponse https://api.example.com/submit post:json x 1 y 2
```

That `post:json` body is `{ "name": "alice", "score": 10 }` (or `{ "x": 1, "y": 2 }` for the `#fetchwith` line).

# Runtime
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/firmware/runtime

For the player-facing list of every `#command`, see [All commands](/firmware#all-commands) (filter by the **R** badge).

**Purpose**: Defines `RUNTIME_FIRMWARE` — commands for runtime messaging, gadget UI, and scroll/text display. Handles the execution context when codepages run during gameplay.

## Lifecycle

`aftertick` processes the gadget queue for the current element:

- **Single string** — If element exists: empty string clears sidebar; else sets tickertext and tickertime (floating ticker only; no chat/tape)
- **Multiple items** — If player: updates shared sidebar with padded content; else: sets scrolllock, scrollname, scroll for the focused player

# Transforms
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/firmware/transforms

**Purpose**: Defines `TRANSFORM_FIRMWARE` — commands for board-level transformations: snapshot/revert, copy, remix, erase, weave, and pivot. Used for level editing and procedural generation.

{/* firmware-catalog:begin */}
{/* Generated by `yarn task docs` (firmware command catalog). Do not edit by hand. */}

<a id="module-commands"></a>

## All commands (7)

<p class="fw-where-legend"> <span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span> CLI - terminal / operator <span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span> Loader - import <span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span> Runtime - codepages </p>

| Command | Where | Description |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| [`#copy`](#copy) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | region from source to current board |
| [`#erase`](#erase) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | board elements by filter (targetset / region) |
| [`#pivot`](#pivot) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | board elements by degrees; optional shear keyword (taper_floor, taper_ceil, taper_trunc, mishin_floor, mishin_ceil, shear_soft, shear_hard) then region / targetset |
| [`#remix`](#remix) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | from source with pattern size and mirror to current board |
| [`#revert`](#revert) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | board to snapshot state |
| [`#snapshot`](#snapshot) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | board snapshot |
| [`#weave`](#weave) | <span class="fw-where-cell"><span class="fw-where fw-where-cli">C</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-loader">L</span><span class="fw-where fw-where-runtime">R</span></span> | board elements in direction |
{/* firmware-catalog:end */}

## Commands

### Board transforms

#### #snapshot

**Args:** —

Calls [`boardsnapshot`](../../feature/boardsnapshot.ts) on the sim — creates MAIN `zss_snapshot_*` codepage and copies current board.

#### #revert

**Args:** —

Calls [`boardrevert`](../../feature/boardsnapshot.ts) on the sim — restores current board from snapshot codepage.

#### #erase

**Args:** [filter…]

Erase matching elements; filter **`<group>`** (optional color) or builtins `all`/`terrain`/`object`.

#### #weave

**Args:** `dir` [filter…]

Weave board; filter **`<group>`** or builtins.

#### #pivot

**Args:** `degrees` [filter…]

Rotate; filter **`<group>`** or builtins. Optional shear keyword (`taper_floor`, `taper_ceil`, `taper_trunc`, `mishin_floor`, `mishin_ceil`, `shear_soft`, `shear_hard`) then region / targetset.

#### #copy

**Args:** `stat` [filter…]

Copy region; filter **`<group>`** or builtins.

The invoking object is preserved (not soft-deleted). Terrain under it still updates; a stamped object is not placed on its cell.

#### #remix

**Args:** `stat` `pattersize` `mirror` [filter…]

Remix; custom filter is group/kind name via `@group` or display name.

Same invoker preservation as `#copy`: the chip that ran `#remix` is not blanked away; terrain under it still updates.

Example:

```
#snapshot
#erase terrain
#weave n object
#pivot 90 all
#copy otherboard
#remix otherboard 4 1
#revert
```

## Filter Grammar

`readfilter` parses optional filter args after command-specific args (`#erase` takes only the filter; `#pivot` / `#weave` / `#copy` / `#remix` parse it after their own args):

- **targetset** — default `all`
- **region** — `x1 y1` (single cell) or `x1 y1 x2 y2` (inclusive corners)
- **region (one token)** — `x1,y1,x2,y2` — same layout as `ptstoarea` / batch selection paths; required so values like `0,0,5,5` are not misread as `parseFloat` → `0` with missing follow-up numbers

Filter controls which elements are affected:

- Built-ins: `all`, `terrain`, `object` (and `self` / `others` where applicable)
- **`<group>`** — optional color prefix; matches `@group` **or** element display name via `memoryreadgroup` / `memorylistelement({ group, self })`

### Builtin targetsets

```
#erase
#erase all
#erase terrain
#erase object
#pivot 90 terrain
#weave n object
```

### Group / display name

```
#erase slime
#erase red key
#pivot 90 wall
#weave e doors
#copy otherboard slime
```

### Region as four numbers

```
#erase 10 5 20 12
#erase terrain 0 0 59 24
#pivot 90 object 5 5 15 15
#weave n all 2 2 8 8
```

### Region as one comma token

Needed when the rect is a single word (selection / paste paths):

```
#erase 0,0,5,5
#erase object 10,5,20,12
#pivot 90 slime 0,0,30,20
#copy otherboard all 0,0,59,24
```

### Combined targetset + region

Order can mix; both are applied:

```
#erase slime 4 4 12 10
#erase 4 4 12 10 slime
#remix otherboard 4 1 terrain 0,0,20,12
```

## pickcodepage

Helper that searches books for a codepage of given type and stat/address (`memorypickcodepage(memoryreadbooklist(), type, stat)`). Used to resolve `stat` in copy/remix to a source board.

## Implementation Notes

- `snapshot` / `revert` call feature modules directly on the sim (same pattern as `#build` → `boardbuild`)
- `weave` uses `READ_CONTEXT.element` position for delta
- `pivot` uses degrees converted to radians
- All commands require READ_CONTEXT.book and READ_CONTEXT.board

---

# Gadget scroll catalog
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/gadget/gadget-scrolls

The right-hand **scroll** panel shows a titled list (`scrollname` + `scroll` rows). This page lists every major code path that fills it.

**State:** [`zss/gadget/data/state.ts`](../data/zustandstores.ts) (`GADGET_STATE.scrollname`, `scroll`).

**Ways content is built:**

1. **Markdown** via [`parsemarkdownforscroll`](../../feature/parse/markdownscroll.ts) (marked → ZeText sink → [`scrollwritelines`](../data/scrollwritelines.ts)). Optional `chip` argument (default `refscroll`) is forwarded to `scrollwritelines`. Used for bundled `refscroll:*` `.md` help prose, ZNS `docs` fallback, and other CommonMark bodies in [`handledefault`](../../device/vm/handlers/default.ts).
2. **Zed line blocks** via [`scrollwritelines`](../data/scrollwritelines.ts): plain lines become strings; lines with `!` and a first raw `;` become hyperlinks (`!command args;$label`). Used for built-in menus (e.g. `refscroll:menu`, zip picker, object/terrain lists).
3. Call [`scrollwritelines`](../data/scrollwritelines.ts) directly when you already have a string of tape lines (same `!` / zsstext rules); default link chip is `refscroll` unless overridden. Prefer composing that string with [`zsstextui`](../../feature/zsstextui.ts) (`zsszedlinkline`, `zsszedlinklinechip`, `zsstexttape`, headers/tables) rather than hand-rolling `!payload;label` rows.
4. Queue lines with [`gadgettext` / `gadgethyperlink`](../data/api.ts), then assign `shared.scroll = gadgetcheckqueue(player)` (and usually set `scrollname`). Still used where panels mix imperative steps, **shared** hyperlink state (`get`/`set`), or firmware-driven queues (see admin / element scroll lock). Inspect menus use [`scrollwritelines`](../data/scrollwritelines.ts) plus [`registerhyperlinksharedbridge`](../data/api.ts) where shared widgets need `get`/`set`.

---

## Scroll builder inventory (scroll panel scope)

This subsection catalogs how the scroll panel is filled: **Category C** (centralized on [`scrollwritelines`](../data/scrollwritelines.ts)), **Category B** (hybrid), and **Category A** (fully imperative). Scope: code that sets `shared.scroll` / `shared.scrollname` on the player gadget. Related but out of this list: ROM gadget line DSL ([`zss/rom/index.ts`](../../rom/index.ts)) and firmware element scroll-lock ([`RUNTIME_FIRMWARE.aftertick`](../../firmware/runtime.ts)).

### Category C — Centralized on `scrollwritelines`

Call sites use [`scrollwritemarkdownlines`](../../feature/parse/markdownscroll.ts) (markdown → Zed lines → `scrollwritelines`) or [`scrollwritelines`](../data/scrollwritelines.ts) directly for raw Zed tape—not loops of `gadgettext`/`gadgethyperlink`. Examples include [`handlegadgetscroll`](../../device/vm/handlers/scroll.ts), [`writezztcontentwait` / `writezztcontentlinks`](../../device/vm/helpers.ts), and the **inspect** family ([`inspection.ts`](../../memory/inspection.ts), [`inspectionbatch.ts`](../../memory/inspectionbatch.ts), [`inspectionremix.ts`](../../memory/inspectionremix.ts), [`inspectionmakeit.ts`](../../memory/inspectionmakeit.ts), [`inspectionstyle.ts`](../../memory/inspectionstyle.ts), [`inspectionfind.ts`](../../memory/inspectionfind.ts)) with `registerhyperlinksharedbridge` for shared hyperlink types. See **VM handler entry points** and **`refscroll:<path>` in `handledefault`** below.

### Category B — Hybrid (imperative prefix, then `scrollwritelines`)

| Flow | Source | Pattern |
|------|--------|---------|
| Bookmarks panel | [`zss/memory/bookmarkscroll.ts`](../../memory/bookmarkscroll.ts) | `gadgethyperlink` (name + SAVE) + `gadgetbbar`, then `scrollwritelines` for URL rows. |
| Editor bookmarks | [`zss/memory/editorbookmarkscroll.ts`](../../memory/editorbookmarkscroll.ts) | `gadgethyperlink` (snapshot) + `gadgetbbar`, then `scrollwritelines` for OPEN/COPY rows. |
| List refscrolls + “back” | [`zss/device/vm/handlers/default.ts`](../../device/vm/handlers/default.ts) | `appendmainmenushortcutafterlistscroll`: one `gadgethyperlink` for main menu, then **append** `gadgetcheckqueue` tail to **existing** `shared.scroll`. |

### Category A — Fully imperative (no `scrollwritelines`)

These modules call `gadgettext` / `gadgethyperlink` in sequence and assign `shared.scroll = gadgetcheckqueue(player)` (usually with `shared.scrollname`).

| Scroll title(s) | Source | Notes |
|-----------------|--------|-------|
| `cpu #admin` | [`zss/memory/utilities.ts`](../../memory/utilities.ts) (`memoryadminmenu`) | Sections + links; `refscroll:adminscroll`. |

### Refactor roadmap (priority tiers)

- **Tier 1** — [`memoryadminmenu`](../../memory/utilities.ts) (`cpu #admin`): mostly plain lines and simple `gadgethyperlink` without custom `get`/`set`; reasonable place to prototype a tape string + one `scrollwritelines`, or `scrollwritelines` for a static body after any imperative header (same idea as bookmarks).
- **Tier 2** — [`bookmarkscroll.ts`](../../memory/bookmarkscroll.ts), [`editorbookmarkscroll.ts`](../../memory/editorbookmarkscroll.ts), [`appendmainmenushortcutafterlistscroll`](../../device/vm/handlers/default.ts): already structured, or they need **append** to existing scroll / **`gadgetbbar`**—not covered by a single plain `scrollwritelines(content)` call.
- **Tier 3** — ~~Inspect modules~~ **done:** inspect scrolls use `scrollwritelines` + `registerhyperlinksharedbridge` for shared types (`select`, `text`, `number`, edits, etc.).

**Blockers for a single `scrollwritelines`:** per-link `get`/`set` without bridges, multiple `gadgetcheckqueue` flush points, **`gadgetbbar`**, appending to an existing scroll, ROM-style layout helpers.

---

## Behavior notes

### Clearing the panel vs unlocking scroll

- [`gadgetclearscroll`](../data/api.ts) sets `scrollname` to `''` and `scroll` to `[]` for that player (local gadget state only).
- [`vmclearscroll`](../../device/api.ts) emits `vm:clearscroll`. The VM handler [`handleclearscroll`](../../device/vm/handlers/scroll.ts) walks the player's board objects and calls [`memoryunlockscroll`](../../memory/runtime.ts) so each chip's **scroll lock** can clear (`scrollunlock` on the element); it also calls `gadgetclearscroll` for the player so the panel empties on the next sim → client gadget patch.

So: **`clearscroll` is not only “clear pixels”** — it also propagates unlocks. **`gadgetclearscroll` alone** only clears stored panel content (no chip unlock).

### Scroll lock (element → player)

In [`RUNTIME_FIRMWARE.aftertick`](../../firmware/runtime.ts), when a **non-player** element’s gadget queue has **more than one** item, the runtime calls `chip.scrolllock(player)` for the focused player, then copies the queue into that player’s `scrollname` / `scroll`. While locked, the chip’s [`message`](../../chip.ts) handler ignores incoming messages from other players (`flags.sk`). Element-driven scroll stays until `vm:clearscroll` (or equivalent unlock path) runs.

### Hyperlink chips

Hyperlink rows are `[chip, label, ...args]` (see [`gadgethyperlink`](../data/api.ts)). The **chip** string is the VM/default-handler branch used when the link is activated (e.g. `refscroll`, `bookmarkscroll`, `zipfilelist`, `list`, `adminop`). Bundled refscroll help content is often markdown on disk; `registerhyperlinksharedbridge` in [`api.ts`](../data/api.ts) can supply `get`/`set` for `HYPERLINK_WITH_SHARED` types (e.g. `zipfilelist` + `select`) so generated links need no per-row closures.

### Where scroll / sidebar messages go

Panel / tape link widgets under [`zss/screens/linkui/`](../../screens/linkui/) emit via `LinkSurface.sendmessage` → [`chipmessage`](../../device/api.ts) / `SOFTWARE.emit` on the main thread. [`shouldforwardclienttoserver`](../../device/forward.ts) forwards these `vm:*` messages to the **sim VM**, where registry-listed handlers (`refscroll`, `gadgetscroll`, `makeitscroll`, `clearscroll`, `bookmarkscroll`, …) and `handledefault` branches run. Chips execute on the sim worker in the same tick as `memorytickmain`.

### Terminal tape vs scroll (shared hyperlinks)

Both surfaces parse bang lines with [`parsezedlinkline`](../../feature/zedlinkparse.ts) (first `;`, `$59` escapes, optional `!@chip`). Widgets are shared under [`zss/screens/linkui/`](../../screens/linkui/). For `HYPERLINK_WITH_SHARED` types, the modem address is `paneladdress(chip, target)` (`chip:target`, target must not contain `:`). Tape lines may carry that key as `!chip:target!command;label` (or `!!…` after terminallog). [`useHyperlinkSharedSync`](../data/usehyperlinksharedsync.ts) registers the same modem observe/init + bridge path for both layouts. [`registerterminalhyperlinksharedbridge`](../data/api.ts) adds tape-only defaults; merged lookup **prefers** `registerhyperlinksharedbridge`.

Full wiring: [scroll-vs-terminal-hyperlinks.md](./scroll-vs-terminal-hyperlinks.md).

### ZNS docs for `refscroll:<path>`

The UI briefly shows title `$7$7$7 please wait` and loading text, then [`fetchrefscrolltext`](../../feature/fetchrefscrolltext.ts) (`docs.at.zed.cafe` → ROM fallback) + [`parsemarkdownforscroll`](../../feature/parse/markdownscroll.ts) fill the panel, or an in-scroll “doc not found” error if both miss.

---

## VM handler entry points

Registered in [`zss/device/vm/handlers/registry.ts`](../../device/vm/handlers/registry.ts).

| Registry key | Handler | Role |
|--------------|---------|------|
| `refscroll` | [`handlerefscroll`](../../device/vm/handlers/scroll.ts) | Loads `refscroll:menu` with title `#help or $meta+h` via [`scrollwritelines`](../data/scrollwritelines.ts). |
| `gadgetscroll` | [`handlegadgetscroll`](../../device/vm/handlers/scroll.ts) | Payload `{ scrollname, content, chip? }` → `scrollwritelines`. API: [`vmgadgetscroll`](../../device/api.ts). |
| `makeitscroll` | [`handlemakeitscroll`](../../device/vm/handlers/scroll.ts) | [`memorymakeitscroll`](../../memory/inspectionmakeit.ts) → title `makeit`. |
| `clearscroll` | [`handleclearscroll`](../../device/vm/handlers/scroll.ts) | Calls [`gadgetclearscroll`](../data/api.ts) to empty the panel on the next gadget patch and walks the player's board objects calling [`memoryunlockscroll`](../../memory/runtime.ts) to release any chip scroll locks. |
| `bookmarkscroll` | [`handlebookmarkscroll`](../../device/vm/handlers/bookmarkscroll.ts) | [`memorybookmarkscroll`](../../memory/bookmarkscroll.ts): header links + `gadgetbbar`, then [`scrollwritelines`](../../gadget/data/scrollwritelines.ts) for list rows. |
| `editorbookmarkscroll` | [`handleeditorbookmarkscroll`](../../device/vm/handlers/editorbookmarkscroll.ts) | [`memoryeditorbookmarkscroll`](../../memory/editorbookmarkscroll.ts): snapshot link + `gadgetbbar`, then `scrollwritelines` for entries. |
| `readzipfilelist` | [`handlereadzipfilelist`](../../device/vm/handlers/zipfile.ts) | Title `zipfilelist`; Zed `!` lines via `scrollwritelines`, chip `zipfilelist`. |

Panel-only actions for editor bookmarks go through [`handledefault`](../../device/vm/handlers/default.ts) as `editorbookmarkscroll:<path>` (e.g. `snapshotcurrent`, `copytogame`, `editorbookmarkdel` → confirm scroll, `editorbookmarkdelconfirm` → `register:bookmark:delete`, `editorbookmarkdelcancel` → restore list from cache). URL bookmark deletes on `bookmarkscroll` use the same confirm / cancel pattern (`bookmarkdel` → prompt, `bookmarkdelconfirm` / `bookmarkdelcancel`). Terminal pin delete (`vm:bookmarkdeleteprompt`) opens the same confirm scroll. DELETE / cancel links use plain `hyperlink` with a leading `next` data word so [`LinkHyperlink`](../../screens/linkui/hyperlink.tsx) skips `sendclose` (same keep-open flag as hotkey `next`) — otherwise `vm:clearscroll` races the replacement scroll and wipes it.

**Tape editor close:** On [`register.ts`](../../device/register.ts) `editor:close`, the UI clears local editor state and calls [`vmtapeeditorclose`](../../device/api.ts), which emits `vm:tapeeditorclose` into the sim worker. There is no dedicated row for that target in [`vmhandlers`](../../device/vm/handlers/registry.ts); it falls through [`handledefault`](../../device/vm/handlers/default.ts) like other unmatched VM subtargets.

**`snapshotcurrent` and `useTape`:** The sim worker does not share the main-thread Zustand [`useTape`](../data/zustandstores.ts) store. `editorbookmarkscroll:snapshotcurrent` is handled in [`handleeditorbookmarkscrollpanel`](../../device/vm/handlers/editorbookmarkscroll.ts): with a code page id in `message.data`, it loads the page via [`memoryreadcodepagebyid`](../../memory/codepages.ts) and calls [`registerbookmarkcodepagesave`](../../device/api.ts). [`registereditoropen`](../../device/api.ts) still runs before `register:editor:open` for editor UI state; closing the editor uses `editor:close` → `vmtapeeditorclose` as above.

---

## `refscroll:<path>` in `handledefault`

Special paths (not necessarily ROM filenames) in [`handledefault`](../../device/vm/handlers/default.ts) `case 'refscroll'`:

| Path | Title | Notes |
|------|-------|--------|
| `adminscroll` | `cpu #admin` | [`memoryadminmenu`](../../memory/utilities.ts). |
| *(any other)* | `path` | Bundled `.md` or ZNS docs; see below. |

Char / color / bg editors are **inline** on [`menu.md`](../../rom/refscroll/menu.md) (`!char charedit`, etc.) — compact until ENTER. Dedicated `charscroll` / `colorscroll` / `bgscroll` paths were removed.

**Default branch:** loading scroll, then [`fetchrefscrolltext`](../../feature/fetchrefscrolltext.ts) (ZNS first, ROM fallback) + `parsemarkdownforscroll`, or error scroll. Final `scrollname` is `path` once content is ready.

---

## ROM keys (`refscroll/`)

Bundled under [`zss/rom/refscroll/`](../../rom/refscroll/) as **`.md`** files. Address = `refscroll:<name>` where `<name>` is the filename without `.md`.

`cliscroll`, `commandsscroll`, `helpcontrols`, `helpdeveloper`, `helpmenu`, `helpplayer`, `helptext`, `menu`, `notesscroll`.

Synth, effects, scales, and TTS voices are Blume pages opened from [`menu.md`](../../rom/refscroll/menu.md): [`voices.md`](../../feature/synth/docs/(play)/voices.md), [`effects.md`](../../feature/synth/docs/(play)/effects.md), [`scales.md`](../../feature/synth/docs/(play)/scales.md), [`tts-voices.md`](../../feature/docs/tts-voices.md).

---

## Inspection and memory flows (`scrollname` values)

These flows are **Category A** in [Scroll builder inventory](#scroll-builder-inventory-scroll-panel-scope): they set `scrollname` while building the gadget queue; several use **shared** hyperlink `get`/`set` (config toggles, find-any text slots) and stay on the queue API until bridged like zip `select` (see source for exact entry points).

---

## Firmware and tools

| Title | Source |
|-------|--------|
| *(element `name` or `kinddata.name`)* | [`RUNTIME_FIRMWARE.aftertick`](../../firmware/runtime.ts) — non-player element, multi-line gadget queue, focused player |
| [`ZZT_BRIDGE`](../../device/vm/helpers.ts) (decorated banner) | [`writezztcontentwait` / `writezztcontentlinks`](../../device/vm/helpers.ts) → `scrollwritelines` (chip `zztbridge`) |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph vm [VM_messages]
    refscroll[refscroll]
    gadgetscroll[gadgetscroll]
    makeitscroll[makeitscroll]
    bookmarkscroll[bookmarkscroll]
    editorbm[editorbookmarkscroll]
    readzip[readzipfilelist]
  end
  subgraph default [handledefault]
    refpath[refscroll_path]
  end
  subgraph fill [Fill_gadget_panel]
    mdscroll[parsemarkdownforscroll]
    apply[scrollwritelines]
    queue[gadgettext_gadgethyperlink_checkqueue]
  end
  refscroll --> apply
  gadgetscroll --> apply
  makeitscroll --> queue
  bookmarkscroll --> apply
  editorbm --> apply
  readzip --> apply
  refpath --> romzns[fetchrefscrolltext_zns_then_rom]
  romzns --> mdscroll
```

# Scroll panel vs terminal tape hyperlinks
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/gadget/scroll-vs-terminal-hyperlinks

This page expands [gadget-scrolls.mdx § Terminal tape vs scroll](./gadget-scrolls.mdx#terminal-tape-vs-scroll-shared-hyperlinks).

## Shared parse model

Both surfaces use [`parsezedlinkline`](../../feature/zedlinkparse.ts):

```text
![@chip ]command args;label
```

| Rule | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| Label separator | **First** raw `;` |
| Semicolon in fragments | `$59` via `scrolllinkescapefrag` / `scrolllinkunescapefrag` |
| Tokens | [`zedlinksplittokens`](../../feature/zedlinkparse.ts) (whitespace + quoted strings) |
| Per-line chip | `!@chipname …;label` |
| Default chip | Second arg to `parsezedlinkline` / writelines (usually `refscroll`) |
| Tape modem prefix | Optional `!chip:target!command;label` (or `!!command;label` after terminallog doubles the bang) |

Authors should build lines with [`zsszedlinkline`](../../feature/zsstextui.ts) / [`zsszedlinklinechip`](../../feature/zsstextui.ts) so escapes stay correct. [`writecopyit`](../../feature/writeui.ts) / [`writehyperlink`](../../feature/writeui.ts) go through `zsszedlinkline`.

## Shared UI widgets

Control widgets live once under [`zss/screens/linkui/`](../../screens/linkui/). Thin routers:

- Tape: [`TerminalItem`](../../screens/terminal/item.tsx) → `parsezedlinkline` → [`resolvelinktypeandwords`](../../screens/linkui/linktypes.ts) → [`LinkRouter`](../../screens/linkui/router.tsx)
- Scroll: [`PanelItem`](../../screens/panel/panelitem.tsx) → unpack `PANEL_ITEM` → same resolve → `LinkRouter`

`charedit` / `coloredit` / `bgedit` stay **compact** until ENTER enters edit focus (BIG grid). `number` / `nm` uses the same ENTER enter / ENTER accept / ESC cancel cycle (ESC reverts the value from edit start). Expanded visual editors reserve height via [`linkediting`](../../screens/linkui/linkediting.ts) + [`linkexpandrowheight`](../../screens/linkui/linktypes.ts); scroll does **not** pin the expanded row to the top.

Surface adapters (`LinkSurface`) carry layout (`terminal` | `panel`), `sendmessage` / `sendclose`, modem prefix / chip, and write-text context. Panel simple links still `sendclose()`; terminal `runit` uses `registerterminalopen` while panel uses `sendclose` + `registerterminalquickopen`.

Panel control striping (`select` / `range` / `number` / `text`) uses one even/odd bg for the whole row lead-in via [`linkpanelstripe`](../../screens/linkui/surface.ts); `iseven` comes from content `striperow` (scroll passes `striperowbase={offset}`), not viewport draw Y.

## Shared modem prefix

For `HYPERLINK_WITH_SHARED` widgets (`select`, `range`, `text`, in-place edits, etc.), the **modem address** must match `paneladdress(chip, target)` — i.e. `chip:target` with **only the first colon** separating chip from target (**`target` must not contain `:`**).

- **Scroll panel:** rows from [`gadgethyperlink`](../data/api.ts); [`useHyperlinkSharedSync`](../data/usehyperlinksharedsync.ts) with `{ chip, target }`.
- **Terminal tape:** modem key in `LinkSurface.modemprefix`; same hook with `{ modemprefix }`.

[`registerterminalhyperlinksharedbridge`](../data/api.ts) supplies tape-only defaults. Merged lookup **prefers** [`registerhyperlinksharedbridge`](../data/api.ts); the terminal registry is used only when no scroll bridge is registered for that `(chip, type)`.

## Primary code references

| Concern | Location |
|--------|----------|
| Shared parse | [`zss/feature/zedlinkparse.ts`](../../feature/zedlinkparse.ts) |
| Shared widgets | [`zss/screens/linkui/`](../../screens/linkui/) |
| Panel stripe helpers | [`zss/screens/linkui/surface.ts`](../../screens/linkui/surface.ts) (`linkbegin`, `linkpanelstripe`) |
| Tape line entry | [`zss/screens/terminal/item.tsx`](../../screens/terminal/item.tsx) |
| Scroll row entry | [`zss/screens/panel/panelitem.tsx`](../../screens/panel/panelitem.tsx) |
| Shared sync | [`zss/gadget/data/usehyperlinksharedsync.ts`](../data/usehyperlinksharedsync.ts) |
| Bridge registration | [`zss/gadget/data/api.ts`](../data/api.ts) |

# Glossary
Source: https://zed.cafe/docs/glossary

Creator-facing terms for boards, books, `#command`s, and the terminal.

**Jump:** [B](#b) · [C](#c) · [D](#d) · [E](#e) · [F](#f) · [G](#g) · [H](#h) · [I](#i) · [J](#j) · [K](#k) · [L](#l) · [M](#m) · [O](#o) · [P](#p) · [R](#r) · [S](#s) · [T](#t) · [W](#w) · [Z](#z)

## B

### bgplay

`#bgplay` plays a short sound-effect pattern on the background synth voices (same notation family as [play](#play)).

Related: [play](#play) · [command](#command)

See: [Synth](/synth) · [Notation](/synth/playnotation)

### board

A playable 60×25 room: terrain, objects, exits, and camera. You walk boards; `#boards` lists them.

Related: [board page](#board-page) · [board element](#board-element) · [book](#book) · [exit](#exit)

See: [Your first board](/guides/first-board)

### board element

One occupant of a board cell — kind, char, color, collision, cycle, and params like [p1–p20](#p1p20). Same idea as [element](#element).

Related: [kind](#kind) · [chip](#chip) · [collision](#collision)

### board page

A [code page](#code-page) that stores a [board](#board) layout inside a [book](#book).

Related: [object page](#object-page) · [terrain page](#terrain-page)

### book

A container of [code page](#code-page)s (boards, objects, terrain, and more). One book is **opened**; new pages go there. `#books` lists them.

Related: [MEMORY](#memory) · [page](#page)

See: [Your first ten minutes](/guides/first-ten-minutes)

## C

### cafe

The Vite/React app shell at zed.cafe that hosts the [Engine](#engine) and [tape](#tape) UI.

Related: [ZED Cafe](#zed-cafe) · [ZSS](#zss)

### charset page

A [code page](#code-page) of custom character glyphs used when drawing the board.

Related: [palette page](#palette-page) · [CRT](#crt)

### chip

The per-element script runner: compiled ZSS, stats, firmware `#command`s, and messages between objects.

Related: [firmware](#firmware) · [label](#label) · [send](#send)

See: [Firmware](/firmware)

### CLI driver

Where terminal `#` input runs. Permission checks apply here (unlike loader / runtime).

Related: [firmware](#firmware) · [tape](#tape) · [command](#command)

### code page

An editable unit inside a [book](#book): board, object, terrain, charset, palette, loader, or txt.

Related: [board page](#board-page) · [object page](#object-page)

### collision

How elements bump: walk, solid, swim, bullet, ghost, and related words used in scripts and the inspector.

Related: [kind](#kind) · [DIR](#dir)

See: [Words — collision](/words/collision)

### color

The 16 foreground colors (plus ON / blink variants) used for chars and `#color`.

Related: [palette page](#palette-page)

See: [Words — color](/words/color)

### command

A hash-prefixed firmware action in the terminal or on a code page — `#goto`, `#play`, `#put`, and the rest.

Related: [firmware](#firmware) · [CLI driver](#cli-driver)

See: [All commands](/firmware#all-commands)

### creative

An `#access` preset: players can explore, code, build, and speak. Persist, bridge, moderation, and roles stay restricted.

Related: [lockdown](#lockdown) · [open](#open) · [operator](#operator)

### CRT

The retro monitor look — post-process effects on the fantasy display.

Related: [Engine](#engine) · [gadget](#gadget)

### cycle

How often a chip wakes (1–255). Lower cycle means the object runs more often.

Related: [chip](#chip) · [halt](#halt)

## D

### DIR

Direction vocabulary for movement and targeting: N/S/E/W, SEEK, FLOW, BY, WITHIN, and friends.

Related: [collision](#collision) · [command](#command)

See: [Words — dir](/words/dir)

## E

### element

Something placed on a [board](#board): terrain fills the floor and walls; objects sit on top and can run code. In source this is often a [board element](#board-element).

Related: [kind](#kind) · [object page](#object-page) · [terrain page](#terrain-page)

### Engine

The React root that boots the platform and draws the R3F terminal scene.

Related: [cafe](#cafe) · [gadget](#gadget)

### exit

A board edge link (`@exiteast`, `@exitwest`, and the other compass exits). Walking off that edge goes to the named [board](#board).

Related: [board](#board) · [board page](#board-page)

See: [Your first board](/guides/first-board)

## F

### fantasy terminal

The product metaphor: boards as worlds, `#command`s as the OS, scrolls as help, tape as the CLI.

Related: [tape](#tape) · [scroll](#scroll) · [ZED Cafe](#zed-cafe)

### firmware

The registry of `#command`s and hooks, composed into CLI, loader, and runtime drivers.

Related: [command](#command) · [chip](#chip)

See: [Firmware](/firmware)

### flag

A named value on a book, element, or player — script state you `#set` and `#if`.

Related: [MEMORY](#memory) · [chip](#chip)

## G

### gadget

The render / UI projection of the world: layers, scrolls, per-player view. `#gadget` toggles the inspector overlay.

Related: [inspector](#inspector) · [layer](#layer) · [tape](#tape)

## H

### halt

Dev stop for chip execution (`#dev`) until cleared.

Related: [cycle](#cycle) · [operator](#operator)

### hyperlink

A choice line inside a [scroll](#scroll): `!label;visible text`. Picking it runs that [label](#label) on the object.

Related: [scroll](#scroll) · [label](#label) · [message](#message)

See: [Your first object](/guides/first-object)

## I

### inspector

Visual edit mode (`#gadget`): pick cells, change stats, copy, find-any, remix.

Related: [gadget](#gadget) · [STAT_TYPE](#stat_type)

See: [Your first board](/guides/first-board)

### itch.io

Publish a build with `#itchiopublish` (operator).

Related: [ZNS](#zns) · [book](#book)

## J

### joincode

Operator starts a multiplayer session and shares a join URL (`#joincode`).

Related: [operator](#operator) · [role](#role)

## K

### kind

The type name of an element — used in `#put`, `#become`, collision, and lookup (`player`, `solid`, `lamp`, …).

Related: [object page](#object-page) · [board element](#board-element)

See: [Words — kind](/words/kind)

## L

### label

A named block in object code (`:touch`, `:shot`, or your own). Messages and links jump here.

Related: [chip](#chip) · [send](#send)

See: [Your first object](/guides/first-object)

### layer

A draw plane in the gadget: tiles, sprites, dither, media, control, and blank.

Related: [gadget](#gadget)

### loader page

A [code page](#code-page) that runs when importing external files (text, JSON, binary, media).

Related: [LOADER driver](#loader-driver) · [firmware](#firmware)

See: [Loader](/firmware/loader)

### LOADER driver

Firmware context for import handlers — no permission checks.

Related: [CLI driver](#cli-driver) · [RUNTIME driver](#runtime-driver)

### lockdown

An `#access` preset: tight build/speaker rules; players get no controlled permission groups.

Related: [creative](#creative) · [open](#open)

## M

### makeit scroll

The [scroll](#scroll) that opens when you type `@` plus a page name. It lists create and edit links for that name.

Related: [scroll](#scroll) · [page](#page) · [object page](#object-page)

See: [Your first object](/guides/first-object)

### MEMORY

The live game state root: books, session, loaders, operator. The sim owns it; join tabs project a view.

Related: [book](#book) · [board](#board)

See: [Memory](/memory)

### message

How objects talk: `name:label` from the CLI, or `#name:label` from code, runs that [label](#label) on matching elements. Built-ins include `:touch`.

Related: [send](#send) · [label](#label) · [chip](#chip)

See: [Your first object](/guides/first-object)

## O

### object page

A [code page](#code-page) that defines reusable object behavior bound by [kind](#kind) name.

Related: [chip](#chip) · [board element](#board-element)

See: [Your first object](/guides/first-object)

### open

An `#access` preset: almost everything allowed for every role; risk still needs `#allow` or operator.

Related: [lockdown](#lockdown) · [creative](#creative)

### operator

The privileged session player — bypasses permission checks.

Related: [role](#role) · [joincode](#joincode)

## P

### p1–p20

Generic numeric slots on a [board element](#board-element) for custom object state.

Related: [flag](#flag) · [chip](#chip) · [stat](#stat)

### page

Everyday name for a [code page](#code-page) inside a [book](#book) — board, object, terrain, loader, palette, charset, or txt.

Related: [code page](#code-page) · [book](#book)

### palette page

A [code page](#code-page) that remaps board colors.

Related: [color](#color) · [charset page](#charset-page)

### play

`#play` schedules melody on the main synth voices. Digits in the string are drums, not octaves — see [Notation](/synth/playnotation).

Related: [bgplay](#bgplay) · [command](#command)

See: [Synth](/synth) · [Notation](/synth/playnotation)

### player

The login [kind](#kind) / object you control. Starter kits ship an object page named `player`.

Related: [kind](#kind) · [object page](#object-page) · [operator](#operator)

## R

### role

Assignable identity (admin, mod, player) with permission grants (`#role`).

Related: [operator](#operator) · [lockdown](#lockdown)

### ROM

Built-in help markdown: refscrolls, editor hints, command docs.

Related: [scroll](#scroll) · [command](#command)

### RUNTIME driver

Firmware context when codepage chips run on a board.

Related: [CLI driver](#cli-driver) · [chip](#chip)

## S

### scroll

An in-world text panel — help, lists, [hyperlink](#hyperlink)s, choices. Not the same as the [tape](#tape) CLI. One plain text line is usually a [ticker](#ticker); two or more open a scroll.

Related: [ROM](#rom) · [label](#label) · [toast](#toast)

See: [Gadget scrolls](/gadget/gadget-scrolls)

### send

A message from one element (or the player) to a [label](#label) or target — the event bus for objects. Players usually say [message](#message).

Related: [chip](#chip) · [label](#label) · [message](#message)

See: [Words — send](/words/send)

### starter kit

A ready-made [book](#book) listed on a fresh session (Quick Start Kit, ZZT Tool Kit, and others). Loading one puts pages into MEMORY so you can play or edit immediately.

Related: [book](#book) · [board](#board)

See: [Your first ten minutes](/guides/first-ten-minutes)

### stat

An `@` field on a page that sets looks or board data — `@char`, `@color`, `@exiteast`, `@startx`, and friends. Different from a [flag](#flag), which is runtime `#set` state.

Related: [object page](#object-page) · [exit](#exit) · [STAT_TYPE](#stat_type)

### STAT_TYPE

Inspector / editor categories for stats: board, object, range, hotkey, charedit, and more.

Related: [inspector](#inspector) · [stat](#stat)

See: [Words — stats](/words/stats)

## T

### tape

The terminal input line and code-editor panel (layout modes top / full / bottom / max).

Related: [CLI driver](#cli-driver) · [fantasy terminal](#fantasy-terminal)

### terrain page

A [code page](#code-page) of background tile kinds for the board terrain layer.

Related: [board page](#board-page) · [kind](#kind)

### ticker

One line of text at the bottom of the view. A single plain line from an object usually shows as a ticker; `$ticker ...` forces that line there.

Related: [scroll](#scroll) · [toast](#toast)

See: [Your first object](/guides/first-object)

### toast

A short pop-up message (`$toast ...`).

Related: [ticker](#ticker) · [scroll](#scroll)

See: [Your first object](/guides/first-object)

### TTS

Text-to-speech (`#tts`, `#ttsengine`) via Piper, Supertonic, or Fish.

Related: [command](#command) · [Synth](/synth)

See: [TTS](/feature/tts)

### txt page

A plain-text notes [code page](#code-page) (`@txt name`). No ZSS execution; ZNS can render markdown and `$` colors.

Related: [ZNS](#zns) · [book](#book)

## W

### words

Shared parsers and enums — color, dir, kind, collision, stats — that firmware and scripts share.

Related: [DIR](#dir) · [color](#color) · [kind](#kind)

See: [Words](/words)

## Z

### ZED Cafe

The product at [zed.cafe](https://zed.cafe/) — fantasy terminal worlds, and the ZSS dialect that extends ZZT-OOP.

Related: [cafe](#cafe) · [fantasy terminal](#fantasy-terminal)

### ZNS

Zed Name Service — publish and list shareable content (`#zns`).

Related: [book](#book) · [itch.io](#itchio)

### ZSS

Zed Software System — the TypeScript monolith: cafe UI, engine, firmware, and CLI.

Related: [firmware](#firmware) · [MEMORY](#memory)

Browse classic ZZT worlds with `#zztsearch` / `#zztrandom`.
